title: Lab 222: Linux Package Management — Advanced
description: The objective of this lab is to develop practical skills in advanced Linux package management using DNF and RPM, including identifying the package manager, inspecting installed packages, searching repositories, displaying package information, determining package installation status, identifying package providers, installing and removing packages, examining RPM metadata, listing package-owned files, determining file ownership, checking for available updates, and inspecting enabled repositories.

lab_objective.description: The objective of this lab is to develop practical skills in managing and inspecting Linux software packages using DNF and RPM.
objectives: Understand the role of DNF as a Linux package manager.
Display and inspect currently installed packages.
Search configured repositories for available packages.
Display detailed package information using DNF.
Determine whether a specific package is installed.
Identify which package provides a command or file.
Understand the relationship between DNF and RPM.
List files installed by an RPM package.
Determine which installed package owns a specific file.
Check the system for available package updates.
Display configured and enabled software repositories.
Remove software packages safely using DNF.
Verify that a package has been removed.
Practice documenting package-management operations using command output.
scenario:
You are working as a Linux system administrator responsible for maintaining software packages on a production server.

Your responsibilities include using DNF to search repositories, inspect installed and available packages, install and remove software, and check for updates. You will also use the RPM utility to inspect package metadata, identify files installed by a package, and determine package ownership of system files.

As part of your package-management responsibilities, you must understand the difference between high-level package management with DNF and package inspection with RPM. You must carefully perform each task and document the required command output for verification.

tasks.title: Identify the Package Manager
steps: Create a lab222_pkg_mgt directory inside your home directory.
Determine which package manager is available on the system.
Display the installed DNF version.
Save the output of the command, including any error or diagnostic message, to /home/your-user-name/lab222_pkg_mgt/package_manager.txt
Hint: dnf --version
Hint: Redirect both standard output and standard error to the file using: > file 2>&1

tasks.title: Display Installed Packages
steps: Display the list of packages currently installed on the system.
Review the package name, architecture, and installed version information.
Save the complete output, including any error or diagnostic message, to /home/your-user-name/lab222_pkg_mgt/installed_packages.txt
Hint: dnf list installed
Hint: Redirect both standard output and standard error to the file using: > file 2>&1

tasks.title: Search for a Package
steps: Search the configured repositories for packages related to nfs-utils.
Review the search results and identify packages related to NFS utilities.
Save the search results, including any error or diagnostic message, to /home/your-user-name/lab222_pkg_mgt/nfs-utils_search.txt
Hint: dnf search nfs-utils
Hint: Redirect both standard output and standard error to the file using: > file 2>&1

tasks.title: Display Package Information
steps: Display detailed information about the nfs-utils package.
Your output must include information such as:
Package name
Version
Architecture
Repository
Size
Summary
Save the output, including any error or diagnostic message, to /home/your-user-name/lab222_pkg_mgt/nfs-utils_info.txt
Hint: dnf info nfs-utils
Hint: Redirect both standard output and standard error to the file using: > file 2>&1

tasks.title: Determine Whether a Package Is Installed
steps: Determine whether the nfs-utils package is currently installed.
Save the appropriate package-listing output, including any error or diagnostic message, to /home/your-user-name/lab222_pkg_mgt/nfs-utils_installed.txt
Hint: dnf list installed nfs-utils
Hint: Redirect both standard output and standard error to the file using: > file 2>&1

tasks.title: Find Which Package Provides a Command
steps: Determine which package provides the curl command.
Save the result,including any error or diagnostic message, to /home/your-user-name/lab222_pkg_mgt/curl_provider.txt
Hint: dnf provides '*/curl'
Hint: Redirect both standard output and standard error to the file using: > file 2>&1
Real-world: Administrators frequently need to identify which package provides a missing command or library.

tasks.title: Install a Package
steps: Install the nfs-utils package.
After installation, verify that the package is installed.
Validate using: dnf list installed nfs-utils
Save the verification output,including any error or diagnostic message, to /home/your-user-name/lab222_pkg_mgt/nfs-utils_install_status.txt
Hint: dnf install nfs-utils
Hint: Redirect both standard output and standard error to the file using: > file 2>&1

tasks.title: Examine an Installed RPM Package
steps: Use the rpm command to display detailed information about the installed nfs-utils package.
The output must show information about:
Name
Version
Release
Architecture
Save the output, including any error or diagnostic message, to /home/your-user-name/lab222_pkg_mgt/rpm_package_info.txt
Hint: rpm -qi nfs-utils
Hint: Redirect both standard output and standard error to the file using: > file 2>&1

tasks.title: List Files Installed by a Package
steps: Use RPM to display the files that belong to the installed nfs-utils package.
Save the output, including any error or diagnostic message, to /home/your-user-name/lab222_pkg_mgt/package_files.txt
Hint: rpm -ql nfs-utils
Hint: Redirect both standard output and standard error to the file using: > file 2>&1

tasks.title: Determine Package Ownership of a File
steps: Use RPM to determine which installed package owns /etc/hostname.
Save the result, including any error or diagnostic message, to /home/your-user-name/lab222_pkg_mgt/hostname_owner.txt
Hint: rpm -qf /etc/hostname
Hint: Redirect both standard output and standard error to the file using: > file 2>&1

tasks.title: Check for Available Updates
steps: Check whether updates are available for packages on the system.
Save the output, including any error or diagnostic message, to /home/your-user-name/lab222_pkg_mgt/available_updates.txt
Hint: dnf check-update
Hint: Redirect both standard output and standard error to the file using: > file 2>&1
Important: dnf check-update may return exit status 100 when updates are available. That is normal.

tasks.title: Display Repository Information
steps: Display the repositories currently configured and enabled on the system.
Save the output, including any error or diagnostic message, to /home/your-user-name/lab222_pkg_mgt/enabled_repositories.txt
Hint: dnf repolist
Hint: Redirect both standard output and standard error to the file using: > file 2>&1

tasks.title: Remove a Package
steps: Remove the nfs-utils package that you installed in Task 7.
Verify that the nfs-utils package is no longer installed.
Validate using: dnf list installed nfs-utils
Save the verification output, including any error or diagnostic message, to /home/your-user-name/lab222_pkg_mgt/nfs-utils_remove_status.txt
Hint: dnf remove nfs-utils
Hint: Redirect both standard output and standard error to the file using: > file 2>&1

completion_message: Congratulations! You have completed Lab 222 - Linux Package Management - Advanced. You used DNF to inspect installed packages, search repositories, display package information, determine package installation status, identify package providers, install and remove software, check for updates, and inspect enabled repositories. You also used RPM to examine package metadata, list files installed by a package, and determine package ownership of a system file. These are essential skills for Linux system administrators responsible for maintaining and troubleshooting software on production systems.
